title: Embedding backlog and worker scaling
purpose: Enqueue a controlled number of chunks (at most 10,000, the instructor-approved vector ceiling) on scholarchain-embedding-jobs and observe SQS depth, embedding-worker task count, throughput, retries and drain time.

environment.note: Terraform output region; no AWS call is made by this manifest.

command_notes: BLOCKED until M13-2 is resolved: no EMR entry point exists yet for the embedding enqueue; SC_ENQUEUE_STEP_ARGS (JSON array) must be supplied by the human once an entry point exists (INFRA-CONTRACTS section 14).
Before the run the human raises ecs_min_tasks/ecs_max_tasks for embedding-worker (max 4) through a reviewed Terraform plan; sample_resources.py runs during the window.

scripts/run-experiment.sh runs this command verbatim (no extra arguments) and does not export its run id. The pipeline script therefore generates its own run id; its record is reports/pipeline/10k/<generated id>/run.json (use that id as --run-id of the collectors). The run-experiment.sh run id names only reports/experiments/<id>/<run>/.
scripts/run-experiment.sh refuses a dirty tree: commit the raw results of the previous experiment first (experiments/README.md, Between experiments).

cost_estimate.basis: Titan Embed v2: 10000 chunks x 300 tokens (ASSUMED) x $0.00002 per 1K = $0.06; Fargate about $0.017 per task-hour; EMR enqueue step share about $0.3

dataset_snapshot.notes: chunks derive from the loaded dblp-10k graph; vector count is reported as actually enqueued

metrics_to_collect: cost-explorer:daily UnblendedCost by SERVICE, credits excluded
stop_conditions: more than 10000 messages would be enqueued
DLQ depth above 50: stop enqueueing and report
queue not drained when duration_cap_seconds is reached: report as not drained, do not extend
cost reaches the cost cap (1.00 USD)
reproduction: bash scripts/run-experiment.sh exp-c-embedding-backlog --run-id <token> with python3 -B experiments/collect/sample_resources.py --experiment-id exp-c-embedding-backlog running for the window; analysis: queue_drain.py, scale_timeline.py
